subject: Creativity
title: Dieter Rams: The 10 Principles of Good Design
description: A quick, practical guide to Dieter Rams: The 10 Principles of Good Design.

hook.text: Jony Ive's Apple designs look like Dieter Rams's Braun products from the 1960s. That's not coincidence — it's reverence.

buildup.text: Rams formulated 10 principles: good design is innovative, useful, aesthetic, understandable, unobtrusive, honest.

discovery.text: His most radical principle: 'Good design is as little design as possible.

twist.text: He designed the Braun T3 pocket radio in 1958. Compare it to the iPod — same proportions, same minimalism, 43 years.

climax.text: At 91, Rams says design has failed — too much waste, too much planned obsolescence.

punchline.text: Good design removes everything unnecessary. What remains is honest.

quiz.question: Which of Rams's principles states design should remove everything unnecessary?
options: Good design is as little design as possible

details.summary: Dieter Rams distilled his design philosophy into ten principles, including good design is innovative, makes a product useful, is aesthetic, makes a product understandable, and is as little design as possible. These principles became the foundation of modern product design.
details.whyItMatters: Rams' principles provide a timeless evaluation framework for design quality. Jony Ive explicitly cited Rams as Apple's primary design influence, connecting Braun appliances from the 1960s to the iPhone.
takeaways: Rams established ten principles that define good design
His Braun products directly influenced Apple's design language
Good design is as little design as possible became an iconic principle

faq.question: What are Rams' ten principles?
faq.answer: Good design is innovative, makes a product useful, is aesthetic, makes a product understandable, is unobtrusive, is honest, is long-lasting, is thorough down to the last detail, is environmentally friendly, and involves as little design as possible.

faq.question: How did Rams influence Apple?
faq.answer: Jony Ive openly acknowledged Rams as his primary influence. Compare Braun's 1960s products with Apple's designs and the visual connection is unmistakable. Rams' philosophy of simplicity, functionality, and minimal decoration runs through every Apple product.
